idiom_name: hand-written <entity>_mapper module over the SQLite C API or libpq
implementation_notes: C has no persistence layer in its standard library, so the mapper is a small module per entity: a load function that steps a prepared statement (sqlite3_prepare_v2 / sqlite3_step / sqlite3_column_*, or PQexecParams / PQgetvalue) and fills a plain domain struct, plus insert and update functions that bind the struct's fields as parameters. The struct stays free of driver types and SQL; the connection handle is passed in or held by a per-entity mapper struct, which is what remains of the classic Mapper object. The full structure has to be hand-written and stays that way - there is no reflection to generate it - so the column-to-field correspondence lives in the mapper's code and in its tests.
pitfalls: The bind and column indices are a positional contract with the SQL: inserting a column in the middle of the SELECT list silently shifts every later field.
Every sqlite3_prepare_v2 needs a matching sqlite3_finalize and every PGresult a PQclear on all paths including errors; the mapper is the only layer that can guarantee it.
There is no reflection, so NULL handling is per field and manual (sqlite3_column_type, PQgetisnull); reading a NULL string as "" erases the difference between absent and empty.
A shared sqlite3* handle is not safe across threads in the default threading mode; give each thread its own connection or serialise mapper calls.
